subject: Manufacturing
summary: arc welding (polarity, power-source and arc characteristics, heat input, duty cycle), gas, resistance, thermit and solid-state welding, weld defects and carbon equivalent, brazing and soldering, powder production, compaction and sintering, and polymer and composite processing (moulding processes, rule of mixtures)

questions.text: Alternating current (AC) is generally preferred for TIG welding of aluminium because
opts: it gives the deepest penetration of all polarities
the electrode-positive half-cycle breaks up the surface oxide film (cathodic cleaning) while the electrode-negative half-cycle keeps the tungsten cool
aluminium cannot carry direct current
AC needs no shielding gas
questions.ans: (B) the electrode-positive half-cycle breaks up the surface oxide film (cathodic cleaning) while the electrode-negative half-cycle keeps the tungsten cool
solution: Concept: Aluminium is covered by a tough, high-melting Al2O3 film that must be removed for the weld pool to fuse.
When the electrode is positive, positive ions bombard the work (cathode) and scrub off the oxide; when it is negative, most heat goes into the work and the tungsten stays cool.
AC combines both effects: (B).
Exam tip: DCEN is used for TIG welding of steels and stainless steels; DCEP would overheat a tungsten electrode.

questions.text: A welding power source has the linear characteristic shown (open-circuit voltage 75 V, short-circuit current 600 A). The arc characteristic is V = 20 + 5l, with l the arc length in mm. The arc length (in mm, round off to one decimal place) that gives the maximum arc power is ______
solution: Concept: On a linear source V = V0(1 − I/Is), the power VI is maximum at V = V0/2 and I = Is/2.
P = I(75 − 0.125I); dP/dI = 75 − 0.25I = 0 → I = 300 A, V = 37.5 V, P<sub>max</sub> = 11.25 kW (see figure).
Exam tip: Pmax = V0Is/4 is a quick check: 75 × 600/4 = 11 250 W.

questions.text: A butt weld is made at 30 V and 250 A with a travel speed of 10 mm/s. If 75 % of the arc energy enters the work, the net heat input per unit length (in J/mm, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Net heat input H = ηVI/v (energy delivered per mm of weld).
Exam tip: Higher heat input lowers the cooling rate, which reduces HAZ hardness but coarsens the grains.

questions.text: In a neutral oxy-acetylene flame, the oxygen needed for complete combustion of acetylene is supplied as follows:
opts: all of it from the oxygen cylinder
2.5 volumes from the cylinder and none from air
1.5 volumes from the cylinder and 1 volume from air
1 volume per volume of acetylene from the cylinder (inner cone) and 1.5 volumes from the surrounding air (outer envelope)
questions.ans: (D) 1 volume per volume of acetylene from the cylinder (inner cone) and 1.5 volumes from the surrounding air (outer envelope)
solution: Concept: Complete combustion: C2H2 + 2.5 O2 → 2CO2 + H2O.
Primary reaction in the inner cone: C<sub>2</sub>H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2CO + H<sub>2</sub> (equal volumes from the cylinders; hottest point ≈ 3200 °C just beyond the cone).
Secondary reaction in the outer envelope: 2CO + H2 + 1.5 O2 → 2CO2 + H2O, with oxygen from the air: (D).
Exam tip: Because the inner zone contains CO and H2, the neutral flame shields the pool from oxidation.

questions.text: In a resistance spot weld, a current of 8 kA flows for 0.15 s through an effective resistance of 120 μΩ. The heat generated (in J) is ______
solution: Concept: Joule heating H = I²Rt.
Exam tip: The contact resistance between the sheets is the largest part of R, which is why the nugget forms at the faying surface.

questions.text: In diffusion bonding (diffusion welding), the joint is formed by
opts: melting a thin filler layer between the parts
a high-velocity impact that produces a wavy interface
atomic diffusion across clean, closely mated surfaces held under pressure at an elevated temperature, without melting
frictional heating produced by relative rotation
questions.ans: (C) atomic diffusion across clean, closely mated surfaces held under pressure at an elevated temperature, without melting
solution: Concept: Solid-state processes join metals without melting the base metal.
In diffusion bonding the surfaces are pressed together at about 0.5–0.8 Tm for minutes to hours; atoms diffuse across the interface and voids close up: (C).
(B) describes explosion welding and (D) friction welding.
Exam tip: Diffusion bonding is used for titanium aerospace parts and for joining dissimilar metals and ceramics.

questions.text: In brazing, the joint clearance is kept small (typically 0.025–0.25 mm) mainly because
opts: the filler metal is drawn into and held in the joint by capillary action
a small gap needs no flux
the base metal melts only in narrow gaps
a large clearance makes the joint too strong
questions.ans: (A) the filler metal is drawn into and held in the joint by capillary action
solution: Concept: Brazing depends on wetting and capillary flow of the molten filler between closely fitting surfaces.
If the gap is too large, capillary forces cannot pull the filler in and the joint strength falls towards that of the filler; too small a gap stops the flow: (A).
A properly brazed thin joint can be stronger than the filler alone, because the joint is constrained by the stronger base metal.
Exam tip: Flux is still needed in most brazing to remove oxides and help wetting.

questions.text: A welding transformer is rated at 250 A for a 60 % duty cycle. The duty cycle at which it may be used at 200 A (in %, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: The heating of the source ∝ I² × duty cycle, so I2D is constant.
Exam tip: The current that may be drawn continuously (100 %) is 250 × √0.6 = 193.6 A.

questions.text: Which one of the following products is a typical application where powder metallurgy is clearly superior to other processes?
opts: Large crankshafts
Thin-walled aluminium beverage cans
Long structural I-beams
Self-lubricating porous bronze bearings
solution: Concept: PM can deliberately leave a controlled, interconnected porosity.
Sintered bronze bearings are vacuum-impregnated with oil (20–30 % porosity) and lubricate themselves in service: (D).
Crankshafts are forged, cans are deep drawn and ironed, and I-beams are rolled.
Exam tip: Other PM-only products: cemented carbide tools, tungsten filaments and porous metal filters.

questions.text: A gear blank with a projected area of 1500 mm² is compacted in a die (see figure) at a pressure of 600 MPa. The press force needed (in kN) is ______
solution: Concept: Compaction force = compaction pressure × projected area of the part normal to the pressing direction.
Exam tip: In single-action pressing the density falls with distance from the moving punch; double-action pressing gives a more uniform density.

questions.text: An iron powder compact has a green density of 6.4 g/cm³. The theoretical density of iron is 7.87 g/cm³. The porosity of the compact (in %, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: Porosity = 1 − (actual density/theoretical density).
Relative density = 6.4/7.87 = 0.8132
Exam tip: Sintering and re-pressing raise the relative density; most structural PM steels are 85–92 % dense.

questions.text: In the atomization of molten metals to make powders,
opts: water atomization gives irregular particles and gas atomization gives nearly spherical particles
both water and gas atomization always give flake-shaped particles
gas atomization gives irregular particles with the best green strength
atomization can be used only for brittle metals
questions.ans: (A) water atomization gives irregular particles and gas atomization gives nearly spherical particles
solution: Concept: Particle shape depends on how fast the droplets freeze compared with how fast surface tension rounds them.
Water quenches droplets very quickly, freezing them in irregular shapes (good interlocking, good green strength); in inert gas they have time to spheroidize: (A).
Spherical powders flow and pack well (used in metal injection moulding and additive manufacturing).
Exam tip: Brittle materials are powdered by crushing/milling; flake powders come from ball milling ductile metals.

questions.text: Which one of the following polymers can be softened by heating and re-shaped several times?
opts: Bakelite (phenol formaldehyde)
Cured epoxy resin
Polyethylene
Vulcanized rubber
solution: Concept: Thermoplastics have linear or branched chains held by secondary bonds that weaken on heating; thermosets and vulcanized rubbers are cross-linked by primary bonds.
Polyethylene is a thermoplastic and can be re-melted and recycled: (C).
Bakelite, cured epoxy and vulcanized rubber decompose rather than melt on heating.
Exam tip: Thermoplastics → injection moulding, extrusion, blow moulding; thermosets → compression and transfer moulding.

questions.text: A unidirectional glass-fibre/epoxy composite has 60 % fibres by volume (E<sub>f</sub> = 72 GPa, E<sub>m</sub> = 3 GPa). Its elastic modulus transverse to the fibres (in GPa, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Loaded across the fibres, the phases carry the same stress (iso-stress): 1/Et = Vf/Ef + Vm/Em.
Et = 7.06 GPa
Exam tip: Along the fibres (iso-strain) E = 0.6 × 72 + 0.4 × 3 = 44.4 GPa; the transverse value is governed by the soft matrix.

opts: continuous fibre-reinforced polymer sections of constant cross-section, such as rods, channels and ladder rails
hollow plastic bottles
thin polymer films
large hollow seamless tanks
questions.ans: (A) continuous fibre-reinforced polymer sections of constant cross-section, such as rods, channels and ladder rails
solution: Concept: In pultrusion, continuous fibre rovings are pulled through a resin bath and then through a heated die that shapes and cures the section.
So it makes constant-section, fibre-reinforced profiles of any length: (A).
Bottles are blow moulded, films are blown, tanks are rotationally moulded or filament wound.
Exam tip: Pultrusion is the composite counterpart of extrusion, but the material is pulled, not pushed, through the die.
